title: improv·artist · biological (Eva Hesse)
mutation_directive: improv artist: biological via Eva Hesse

improv_extras.practice: latex, fiberglass, organic asymmetry; cellular hanging forms

v1.feedback: The hanging-strand grid reads as a Hesse-like cellular curtain and the catenary droop + asymmetric bulge show the idea driving the geometry, not just noise. However, a 12×12 uniform grid of cells feels too regular — Hesse's installations (Contingent, Sans II) cluster irregularly with gaps and overlap; randomizing cell placement and varying cluster density would sell the biological read. The warm latex palette is well-chosen but the two-color mix is nearly monotone on screen — adding a third translucent milky-white tone at strand tips would evoke fiberglass resin and add depth. The camera radius of 26 with a 38° FOV leaves a lot of empty warm-beige canvas around the form; tighten the FOV to ~28° or pull the camera to radius ~18 so the hanging field fills more of the frame.

v2.feedback: The hanging catenary strands with organic bulges and latex/resin palette genuinely channel Hesse's cellular curtain forms — the biological brief lands. The gentle sway animation is well-calibrated (calm, earned). Two issues: the piece reads as a field of disconnected hanging threads rather than coherent cellular units — Hesse's work has membrane-like enclosures and clustered pod shapes, not just dangling filaments. Adding lateral connections between nearby strands (web-like bridging lines) or closed-loop cell membranes around each cluster would push it from 'organic scatter' to 'Hesse cellular.' The warm amber palette is restrained and appropriate but could use one cooler translucent note (pale grey-green fiberglass) for depth contrast.
